h: Raising Every Soul to Its Root in Holiness

p: שְׂאוּ אֶת רֹאשׁ כָּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
"Take a census of the entire assembly of the Bnei Yisrael
according to their families, by their fathers' house,
בְּמִסְפַּר שֵׁמוֹת כָּל זָכָר לְגֻלְגְּלוֹתָם (בְּמִדְבַּר א, ב)
by the number of names, every male, by their heads" (Bamidbar 1:2).
הֵבִיא הָרַמְבַּ״ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה מִפֵּירוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י
the Ramban, of blessed memory, cited from Rashi's commentary,
from the expression "Pharaoh will lift off" (Bereishis 40:19)
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי בְּשֵׁבֶט לֵוִי כְּתִיב פְּקוֹד
And for that reason with the tribe of Levi it is written "pekod" (Bamidbar 3:15).
וְהִקְשָׁה הָרַמְבַּ״ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה לְפִי זֶה
And the Ramban, of blessed memory, asked, according to this:
in the census of those who entered the Land,
לָמָּה כְּתִיב שְׂאוּ וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר כו, ב)
And he cited the Midrash Rabbah, Vayikra,
which expounds it as an expression of raising the head:
אֵין שְׂאוּ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן גְּדוּלָּה כּוּלֵּי
just as I have a raised head,
'and You are exalted as head over all,'
so too I have given you a raised head";
But in truth one can interpret it
if they are worthy they will rise to greatness,
and if not, they will all die.
And therefore it is possible to explain
why it says in Parshas Pinchas
since the yetzer hara could still
and it could be, Heaven forbid,
as with the generation that left Mitzrayim,
it was fitting to write the expression "se'u,"
which can be expounded either way.
Now Moshe and Aharon were commanded
to raise up the horn of Yisrael
in all of the ten Sefiros, up to Atika.
And this is what it says, "by their fathers' house,"
of which the Avos are the chariot.
who correspond to Netzach and Hod,
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין יט, ב)
"'The generations of Aharon and Moshe' (Bamidbar 3:1), etc.:
whoever teaches his fellow's son Torah,
as if he had begotten him."
And Moshe and Aharon were the teachers of Yisrael:
מֹשֶׁה הוֹרִיד כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לָאָרֶץ
Moshe brought down all the words of Torah to the earth,
and Aharon brought them close to the Torah.
Moshe is the groomsman of the King
and Aharon the groomsman of the Queen
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג כ, א וְשָׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת)
and therefore they too are called fathers.
יוֹסֵף אִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א קעו, ב)
Yosef: it is stated in the holy Zohar (I 176b):
and so Yosef too is called a father,
and all Yisrael are called by his name:
וְהֵם גַּם כֵּן בִּכְלַל לְבֵית אֲבוֹתָם
and they too are included in "by their fathers' house."
It emerges that in the expression "by their fathers' house"
of the entire assembly of the Bnei Yisrael":
that is, up to Keser Elyon.
And this is the meaning of
"by the number of names, by their heads":
"their heads" indicates up to the root,
And this is why it says with the tribes of Reuven and Shimon
Moshe Rabbeinu needed to raise up specially,
and Yaakov Avinu rebuked them in his blessings.
And likewise the expression "by the number of names"
for the name of every person
is the root of his life,
as is written in the holy sefarim:
"a living soul" — that is his name.
And it says, "according to their families,"
and likewise it says in the count,
יֵשׁ לוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ
One may say that this is what is said afterward,
"And they declared their pedigrees according to their families,"
וְהָרַמְבַּ״ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה הִקְשָׁה עַל זֶה
And the Ramban, of blessed memory, raised a difficulty on this,
and wrote that it does not seem
that witnesses and a document of lineage would be required.
it is possible to explain "And they declared their pedigrees according to their families"
as the effort on the part of man;
and this is the intent of Rashi, of blessed memory:
to bring their books of lineage.
And this corresponds to the middah of Malchus,
the Shabbos of Erev Shabbos night,
which is yirah, and yirah rests in it:
רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה יִרְאַת ה׳ (תְּהִלִּים קיא, י)
"The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem" (Tehillim 111:10);
and this is from the side of man:
מָה ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ שׁוֹאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ וְגוֹ׳ (דְּבָרִים י, יב)
"What does Hashem your God ask of you" etc. (Devarim 10:12).
And this is the meaning of "their generations":
to repair the root of the blemish in one's birth:
(Midrash Rabbah, beginning of Parshas Tazria, Vayikra Rabbah 14:5)
"and in sin did my mother conceive me" (Tehillim 51:7).
And this is the "counsel of the serpent":
that even the most pious of the pious, etc.
And as we said about what we say:
"Roshei Chodashim You have given to Your people,
a time of atonement for all their generations":
for then is the time to repair the root of the blemish,
מֵהַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁהֵטִיל זוּהֲמָא בְּחַוָּה (שַׁבָּת קמו, א)
from the serpent who cast impurity into Chavah (Shabbos 146a).
And this is the effort on the part of man.
And therefore in the census of those who entered the Land, too,
of the entire assembly of the Bnei Yisrael";
to raise the head of the Bnei Yisrael
to be clarified in all ten Sefiros.
And this raising of the head
הוּצְרַךְ לִהְיוֹת עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן
had to be through Moshe and Aharon
and the Nasi of each tribe,
who are the root of the holiness of Yisrael.
This is not so with the tribe of Levi:
they did not need the raising of the head,
וְלָכֵן כְּתִיב פְּקוֹד אֶת בְּנֵי לֵוִי
and therefore it is written, "Count the sons of Levi" (Bamidbar 3:15),
and it does not also write
"by the number of names, by their heads"
And likewise in the census of those who entered the Land
it does not write "by the number of names, by their heads,"
of the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
which is in every one of Yisrael;
we call her Torah she'b'al peh."
שְׂאוּ אֶת רֹאשׁ כָּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
"Raise the head of the entire assembly of the Bnei Yisrael."
אָמַר לְשׁוֹן כָּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
It uses the expression "the entire assembly of the Bnei Yisrael,"
רָאוּי לִנְשִׂיאַת רֹאשׁ עַד כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן
is fit for the raising of the head up to Keser Elyon,
through which one merits the revelation of Atika:
when they accept upon themselves the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven
at the meal of Erev Shabbos night,
"The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem"
they then merit the revelation of Atika
to be clarified up to the root,
